page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local NVMe storage bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific single-threaded and cryptographic workloads. The instance achieved strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 33.6 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.85 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2074.0. Cryptographic performance is also notable, with a strong Passmark CPU encryption test result of 35678.6. Multi-core performance aligns with average expectations for this hardware class, as demonstrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 15951.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 35034.78. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only large block transfer rate of 162.39 GB/sec and a write rate of 83.85 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7i-flex.8xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that require modern Intel instruction sets without the premium of fully dedicated high-memory configurations. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 flags provides hardware-level acceleration for machine learning inference and data processing, as evidenced by a strong text generation speed of 286.26 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM model. This instance is well-suited for batch processing, web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale database operations.
